payload.host_selection: 30 of 105 resample-0 test hosts with >= 2 labelled sites, numpy default_rng(20261008).choice without replacement
payload.pass_note: flag sweep over the labelled sites of each host only; the all-O-atom sweep (sd_all_O) was not run in this pass (CPU time on battery power) and is None

payload.verdict: B: no implementation error; flag effect is a learned outcome at small budgets
payload.verdict_reason: No implementation error found. The flag reaches the output in every checkpoint and in untrained models of both poolings (mean |flag on - flag off| 3.6e-4 to 2.3e-3 eV at init); trained checkpoints reproduce the stored GPU predictions on the CPU (max difference 1.8e-4 eV). Within-host prediction spread is not carried by the flag itself: for S the SD across a host's labelled sites is the same with the flag on and off at every budget; it comes from the environment-dependent embedding of the read-out vacancy node. At initialisation that spread is about 2e-8 eV for every checkpoint's hyperparameters (both poolings), so it is absent at init rather than learned away. After training it is 2.8e-5 to 4.3e-4 eV at B = 25-200 and 1.7e-2 and 6.6e-2 eV at B = 400 and 654 (median target SD 0.121 eV). D's spread comes from the site descriptors: with host-mean site descriptors it is 8e-6 to 2.2e-4 eV at every budget. Budget is confounded with the anchor hyperparameters (set2set/128 at B <= 200, mean/64 at B >= 400 for S); no causal attribution is made. Pass: labelled sites only; the all-O-atom sweep is outstanding.
